payload.statement: In the Q4_K/Q5_K-only template mul_mat_qX_K_q8_2_X4_T (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/iqk/iqk_gemm_kquants.cpp:795), the sampled-profile hot expert kernel (30.16% of user cycles across the <1>/<2>/<3> specializations; the MUL_MAT_ID path, 41.04% wall share in the sibling node profile), the per-128-weight activation scale/dmin conversion is recomputed for every weight row inside the outer ix loop: per (i, iy) it loads 16B of fp16 d[4]/dmin[4] from q8.y[iy][2*i+j], runs the vpmovzxwd/vpmovsxwd/vinserti32x4/cvtepi16 conversion chains and the d x dmin multiplies (~24-27 of the ~87 instructions of each 256-weight block, verified in the installed DSO disassembly of <DequantizerQ4K_AVX2,1> at 0x154760-0x15488a), even though these values depend only on the activation column iy and block i, not on the weight row ix. Mechanism: hoist that conversion into a pre-pass before the ix loop that materializes, per (iy, i), the 8 float scales (dy) and 8 float scale x dmin products (my) into a small per-thread L1-resident buffer (nrc_y x nb x 2 x 32B, <=32KB for this model's contraction dims); the inner loop then replaces the conversion chains with two 16B loads per (i, iy), cutting the per-block instruction count of the weight-streaming inner loop by ~25-30% and removing the fp16-conversion latency from the critical path of the batched-verify specializations where the cost is multiplied by nrc_y. No arithmetic changes: every scale product is computed with the identical operations, once instead of nrc_x times, so results are bit-identical; only which loop computes a value moves. The operator's canonical roofline measurement left 6-20% headroom below the DRAM streaming ceiling on the expert path, so if this kernel is not already at the ceiling the reduced instruction/latency pressure should raise achieved bandwidth; if it is at the ceiling the effect is null and that is the falsifier outcome.
